Hey Dark Eyed One,

I am by no means an expert and this is 100% OPINION based. I would focus on what is going to help you first. Definitely worry about the girl and find out how you and your husband can help but priority #1 has to be to yourself and to going back to feeling normal. When you choose to discuss your past and your issues with folks, you are doing so of your own accord and are mentally prepared to deal with the feelings and the conversation. When something similar is brought up to you in a different context, not only are you not choosing to have the conversation, you're also not prepared for the conversation and the emotions it will bring. You're essentially being caught off-guard, which is going to trigger PTSD or PTSD-like symptoms.

To that end, it makes sense that you're experiencing nervous behaviors, insomnia, and insecurity, even if it seems like there's no cause for it.

I think it's a great idea to encourage your SO to be there for his friend, especially if he was able to do that for you and you know it helped you.

I would not recommend reaching out to this friend yourself until you are absolutely ready to do so. It's fantastic that you would even consider doing this at some point, and speaks volumes to your character, your SO's character (for all the assistance he's given), and to your relationship with each other that you would want to help his friend deal with this. However, it's not something you should undertake until you know you are ready to deal with it. Having these discussions with her will have an impact on you and it may be negative, so you need to make sure you're in the best place mentally to deal with it before you begin.

Talk to your SO about your feelings. Explain to him that you want him to be able to help her, that you are completely ok with it and even encourage it, but that his discussions with you on the situation (especially out of the blue) are actually having a negative impact on you. Let him know that the unexpected broaching of the subject is leading to negative feelings in you and that you need to work these out. Maybe suggest that if he'd like to have a conversation with you about this, he can ask you ahead of time if you can sit and discuss the friend's situation at a time and place you're comfortable with. If you are in control of the conversation and situation, it may help ease the uneasy feelings and the insomnia. I would highly recommend having any conversations like this during a time that you feel safe and secure - maybe while you're curled up in bed together, or out hiking or exercising (working on that physical strength; you need to be strong in every sense to protect yourself).

Very often in shitty relationships, the issue is feeling like there is a loss of control and no protection. You need to know that you have control of your life and that you can keep yourself protected; once you realize these things (and remind yourself daily!) you may be better equipped to talk to your SO's friend and help her in her situation.

Always remember you are an awesome person. You are worthy of love and respect. No one gets to tell you any different, or make you feel any less.
